subject.title: fix(backup): sweep stale temp artifacts before creating new backup

question: Should `backup create` automatically delete one-hour-old OpenClaw-owned staging dirs and archive temp files at startup, or should that cleanup remain manual or doctor-driven?
rationale: The code repair is mechanical, but the destructive cleanup policy changes what old partial backup artifacts mean for operators and should be accepted by an owner before merge.

options.title: Accept Guarded Startup Cleanup
options.body: Repair the matcher, keep the one-hour grace plus owner guards, and treat old OpenClaw temp backup artifacts as disposable crash leftovers.

options.title: Make Cleanup Explicit
options.body: Move the cleanup to a doctor/fix or explicit command path so startup never deletes old backup artifacts automatically.

options.title: Defer The Policy
options.body: Pause this PR until backup artifact retention, diagnostics, and cleanup ownership are clarified.

recommendation.title: Accept Guarded Startup Cleanup
recommendation.body: Repair the matcher, keep the one-hour grace plus owner guards, and treat old OpenClaw temp backup artifacts as disposable crash leftovers.

likelyOwner.reason: They merged and refactored the original backup CLI behavior and are the strongest owner signal for the cleanup policy boundary.
